Consult Summary:
- Young adult with known asthma presenting with 2–3 days of exertional shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough; clinician suspects a small asthma exacerbation and advised interim inhaler adjustments with planned face-to-face GP review.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough for 2–3 days, first noted while running; now provoked by brisk walking.
  - No sputum production.
  - Blue (salbutamol) inhaler reported as not effective for current symptoms.
- Timeline / progression:
  - Symptoms began approximately 2–3 days ago during a run.
  - Symptoms are current and described as worse than baseline (asthma previously controlled).
  - Last significant asthma attack ~3–4 years ago.
  - Last nurse asthma review ~2 years ago.
- Exacerbating / relieving factors:
  - Exertion (running, brisk walking) provokes symptoms.
  - Using blue inhaler as needed; patient and clinician discussed increasing preventer dose.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Wheeze and cough only; no sputum, no fevers or other systemic symptoms documented.
  - Patient reports hay fever (allergic rhinitis).
  - Patient reports possible eczema (uncertain).
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No hospital admissions for asthma reported.
  - No recent oral steroids or antibiotics for asthma recalled.
  - No medication allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma — history of intermittent exacerbations; generally controlled until current episode.
  - No hospital admissions for asthma documented.
  - No history of oral steroid courses documented (patient reports none).
- Allergic rhinitis (hay fever) — patient reports.
- Possible eczema — patient uncertain; family history of eczema.
- Medications explicitly mentioned:
  - Salbutamol (blue inhaler) — dose/route/frequency not fully documented (patient uses as needed; also noted using daily morning/evening in places).
  - Clenil (brown inhaler; inhaled corticosteroid) — patient reports using twice daily; prior/typical dose referenced by clinician as "three puffs twice a day" (see conflict/uncertainty below).
  - Cetraben (emollient) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Hydrocortisone (topical) — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
- Address confirmed during consult: 28 Great Road SW19 1EZ.
- Smoking, alcohol, and recreational drug use: not mentioned / not documented.
- Occupation, living situation, or other social details: not discussed.

Family History:
- Brother: asthmatic.
- Sister: eczema.
- No other family history details provided.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: none documented.
- Examination findings: none documented (planned chest examination at face-to-face review).

Investigations:
- Peak flow:
  - Patient reports a usual/normal peak flow around 380 L/min when well.
  - No current peak flow reading documented during this consult.
- No imaging, lab tests, or other investigations documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute asthma symptoms / probable small asthma exacerbation
  - Assessment: Recent onset (2–3 days) of exertional dyspnea, wheeze, and cough; salbutamol reported as not adequately relieving symptoms. Clinician describes this as a "small exacerbation."
  - Plan:
    - Arrange face-to-face GP review in the next few days for chest examination and peak flow measurement.
    - Interim medication advice:
      - Continue salbutamol (blue inhaler) as required; can be used up to every 2–4 hours temporarily (noted that using this frequently suggests severe asthma).
      - Increase Clenil (brown inhaler) to 4 puffs twice daily while awaiting review (patient had been using twice daily; clinician advised increase).
    - If breathing worsens before review, attend Accident & Emergency (A&E) rather than waiting for the appointment.
    - At face-to-face review, consider oral steroids and/or antibiotics depending on clinical assessment and investigations (clinician stated these may be required depending on findings).
- Issue 2: Asthma control / preventer therapy review
  - Assessment: Asthma review overdue (last nurse review ~2 years ago) and current control suboptimal.
  - Plan:
    - Book and attend an in-person asthma review with GP/nurse (examination, peak flow, medication reconciliation, and optimization).
    - Reassess inhaler technique and adherence at review (implicit in planned review).
- Issue 3: Atopic conditions (hay fever, possible eczema)
  - Assessment: Patient reports hay fever and possible eczema; family history of eczema.
  - Plan:
    - No specific new treatment changes documented for these conditions in this consult.
    - Topical Cetraben and hydrocortisone are listed as current treatments (dose/route/frequency not documented).

General plan items:
- Escalation instructions: attend A&E if breathing deteriorates before scheduled GP review.
- Follow-up: patient to book and attend face-to-face appointment; GP to perform chest exam, peak flow, and decide on need for oral steroids/antibiotics.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Current vital signs (respiratory rate, heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, temperature) not documented.
  - Current peak flow measurement not documented.
  - Exact current doses, routes, and frequencies for salbutamol, Clenil, Cetraben, and hydrocortisone are incompletely documented.
  - Medication adherence and inhaler technique not objectively assessed.
  - Smoking, alcohol, and occupational exposures not documented.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Frequency of blue (salbutamol) inhaler: patient alternatively stated using it "as and when" and also "every day, morning or evening to prevent it" — conflict noted.
  - Patient initially listed medications as "Salbutamol, Flanel Bactroban and Hydrocortisone" then corrected to "Cetraben and Hydrocortisone" — medication list clarified but initial discrepancy noted.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Audio transcript contains some overlapping/unclear segments and hesitations but clinical content (onset, symptoms, medications, and advice) is generally understandable and extractable.
